heading: More
intro: You don't need anything here for everyday use. Come here to see how the agent works, or to adjust it.

memory.title: What it remembers
memory.description: What you told it and what it guessed. Delete anything.

skills.title: Methods it uses
skills.description: How it breaks down goals and estimates time. All swappable.

experiments.title: Experiments
experiments.description: Find out whether a way of working suits you

history.title: Change history
history.description: Everything the agent changed, and a way to undo it

memory.intro: What you told it and what it guessed are kept apart. If a guess is wrong, delete it and it won't be used again.

skills.intro: These are the methods the agent uses when it plans for you. No method suits everyone, so turn off any that don't fit.
skills.tip: To change the details, just tell the agent, for example “count my commute when you estimate time”.
skills.proposal: The agent wants to change this method
skills.addHint: Add methods from GitHub, an archive, or this computer, or write your own.
skills.name: Name
skills.modified: You edited this method. Updating will overwrite your changes.
skills.removeHint: You can undo this in Change history.
skills.binaryUndo: Attached binary files are not covered by undo.
skills.programs: This method includes programs. Jezo’s agent cannot run programs yet; it only follows the instructions.
skills.installed_one: Installed “{{title}}” with {{count}} file. The method is on.
skills.installed_other: Installed “{{title}}” with {{count}} files. The method is on.
skills.nextConversation: It will be used from the next conversation.

experiments.intro: Want to know whether something works for you? The agent alternates two kinds of weeks and tells you what it found.

adopt.label: Plan this way for two weeks
adopt.reply: OK. The next two weeks follow this, and I'll ask how it felt afterward.

rerun.label: Test again
rerun.reply: OK, two more weeks. This time I'll keep the number of meetings about the same in both.

drop.label: Not interested
drop.reply: OK, dropping it. The results stay in the record.

history.intro: The agent’s changes and methods you removed are here. You can undo them.
history.retried_one: Took {{count}} retry to get the format right
history.retried_other: Took {{count}} retries to get the format right
history.claimedWithoutChange: A check caught this, and the next retry worked
history.kept_one: Undone. You changed {{count}} file afterward, so it was left alone.
history.kept_other: Undone. You changed {{count}} files afterward, so they were left alone.

connections.intro: Once connected, calendar events show up on the Calendar page, and runs and flashcard reviews count as done automatically.
connections.outside: Content from outside is marked with where it came from and kept apart from what you say, so it never becomes instructions for the agent.
connections.local: What it reads stays in the workspace on this computer. Jezo doesn't send it anywhere else.
connections.browser: Your browser opens next so you can sign in.

calendars.title: Calendars
calendars.macDetail: Every account added to this Mac shows up: iCloud, Google, Exchange…
calendars.macDenied: macOS hasn't let Jezo read your calendars. Turn Jezo on in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Calendars.
calendars.failed: Can't read it, showing the last copy: {{error}}
calendars.subscribeHint: Paste the calendar's address, and Jezo will read it every so often.
calendars.name: Name
calendars.namePlaceholder: Leave empty to use the calendar's own name
calendars.readOnly: Jezo only reads your calendars; it never changes them.
calendars.macLive: Always up to date with this Mac
calendars.googleDetail: Connects your Google account directly, not through this Mac's calendars. The first time takes about 5 minutes, making a key of your own at Google.
calendars.googleReady: Connects with the key you made at Google; your calendar comes straight from Google to this computer.
calendars.googleIntro: Jezo doesn't go through any service in between, so it uses a key you make at Google (an OAuth client). You do it once; it takes about 5 minutes. Follow each link and do the step at Google:

api.link: Turn on the Google Calendar API

consent.then: : click Get started, name the app Jezo, choose External, and give your own email.

publish.then: : under Audience, click Publish app so it's In production. Otherwise you'd have to connect again every 7 days. It doesn't need review.

client.then: : choose Desktop app, then paste its client ID and secret below.

calendars.googleUnverified: Your browser opens next. Google will say the app isn't verified: it's your own app, so click Advanced, then Go to Jezo. The key and the sign-in stay in this Mac's keychain.
calendars.googleDone: You're connected. Close this tab and go back to Jezo.
calendars.googleFailedPage: That didn't connect. Go back to Jezo to see what happened.
